name: Zhi (Jane) Li
title: Associate Professor
researchAreas: Robot teleoperation and human capability modeling
fitReason: Direct physical HRI and software-method overlap: learning operator capabilities, allocating failure-recovery assistance, and designing shared-autonomy interfaces. A focused algorithm or interface-evaluation contribution could be suitable for CS-oriented methods; hosting and eight-week scope are unconfirmed.

physicalEvidence.summary: The February 2026 primary ARFA paper uses WPI's physical IONA nursing-assistant platform: Kinova Gen3 arm, Robotiq gripper, Freight mobile base and RGB-D cameras. Twenty participants worked in local/remote pairs using HoloLens and a screen interface. The task and failures simulate nursing scenarios on real hardware; this is not a clinical patient-care deployment. Operator capability beliefs learned from performance guide adaptive allocation.

shortVisit.summary: The full live HiRo homepage advertises projects for prospective PhD students and master's thesis students. It does not explicitly invite external summer visitors or internships, specify duration, or establish summer 2027 funding. The lab is physically located in WPI's Unity Hall, but visitor access requires separate host and institutional approval.

scoreReasons.fit: strong adaptive shared-autonomy and human-modeling methods.
scoreReasons.physical: explicit local robot setup and real-user experiment.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: only degree/thesis recruitment, no external visitor route.
scoreReasons.freshness: February 2026 primary study. Provisional fit/evidence score, not acceptance probability or prestige.
